title: The Heath Before Battle
canonical_reference: Inspired by Act 1, Scene 1; this atmospheric framing is original game text.
summary: A storm gathers over Scotland as the generals ride toward Forres.
opening_narration: The wind scours the heath. I ride beneath a bruised sky, while thunder rolls over the battlefield behind us.

available_choices.description: Ride on toward Forres with Banquo.
Pause and study the strange lights on the heath.

title: Fair Is Foul
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 1, Scene 3 (adapted situation; original game narration).
summary: The sisters hail Macbeth with titles and prophecy; their words unsettle both men.
opening_narration: I hear the sisters name me Thane of Cawdor, then king hereafter. Their words strike like a blade laid gently against the mind.

available_choices.description: Tell Banquo you will take the prophecy seriously.
Keep your thoughts to yourself and ride for Forres.

title: News at Forres
canonical_reference: Inspired by Macbeth, Act 1, Scene 3; alternate dialogue and choices are original game content.
summary: Duncan's welcome gives Macbeth a chance to speak openly with Banquo.
opening_narration: Duncan greets me with honor. Banquo watches my face; between us, the prophecy no longer feels like a private dream.

available_choices.description: Ask Banquo to help you judge the prophecy wisely.
Send Lady Macbeth a measured account of the prophecy.

title: A Private Omen
canonical_reference: Alternate-history scene created for this game; it is not Shakespeare's canonical text.
summary: Keeping the prophecy secret leaves Macbeth alone with his growing suspicion.
opening_narration: I conceal the sisters' words. In the quiet passage, every footfall sounds like someone already knows.

available_choices.description: Write Lady Macbeth the truth before doubt hardens.
Leave Forres without telling anyone.

title: A Friend's Warning
canonical_reference: Alternate-history scene created for this game; it is not Shakespeare's canonical text.
summary: Banquo counsels patience, and Macbeth must choose whether to heed him.
opening_narration: Banquo speaks of evil instruments telling small truths to win great harm. I listen, with the crown's shadow still before me.

available_choices.description: Resolve to wait and let events prove themselves.
Thank Banquo, but keep the crown in your thoughts.

title: A Letter at Inverness
canonical_reference: Inspired by Macbeth, Act 1, Scene 5; the letter and choices are original game text.
summary: Macbeth's news reaches Inverness, where Lady Macbeth considers how to answer.
opening_narration: The letter travels north. I imagine Lady Macbeth reading each line by candlelight, weighing what I have not yet dared to say aloud.

available_choices.description: Answer the news with caution and wait for Duncan's next move.
Let ambition guide your next steps together.
Prepare for Duncan's arrival and decide what kind of ruler you will become.

title: The Road Alone
canonical_reference: Alternate-history scene created for this game; it is not Shakespeare's canonical text.
summary: Macbeth travels alone, having left the prophecy unspoken.
opening_narration: I ride north alone. The secret keeps pace beside me, and the road offers no counsel.

available_choices.description: End this chapter in solitude, with the choice unresolved.

title: A Patient Crown
canonical_reference: Alternate-history ending created for this game; it is not Shakespeare's canonical text.
summary: Macbeth chooses patience, leaving the future open rather than forcing the prophecy.
opening_narration: I let the prophecy wait. Scotland's next day is uncertain, but for this night my hand is still my own.

title: The Crown's Shadow
canonical_reference: Alternate-history ending created for this game; it is not Shakespeare's canonical text.
summary: Macbeth and Lady Macbeth choose to pursue power, setting a dangerous alternate path in motion.
opening_narration: Together we turn toward the crown. The choice is ours, and so will be the cost.

title: Unspoken Future
canonical_reference: Alternate-history ending created for this game; it is not Shakespeare's canonical text.
summary: Macbeth ends the chapter carrying a secret that no one else can challenge.
opening_narration: I ride into the dark with the prophecy unshared. What becomes of it is mine to discover another day.

title: A Dagger in the Air
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 1 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth waits for the signal while the image of a dagger sharpens his conflict between ambition and conscience.
opening_narration: I wait beneath the roof that welcomes Duncan. A blade seems to hang before me, though no hand holds it.

available_choices.description: Follow Lady Macbeth's plan and go to Duncan's chamber.
Refuse the murder and wake Duncan before the plan can proceed.

title: Blood on the Hands
location: Duncan's chamber and the adjoining passage
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 2 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Duncan is dead. Macbeth returns shaken, while Lady Macbeth tries to control the evidence and the household.
opening_narration: The deed is done. I hear every sound as an accusation, and the blood on my hands seems impossible to wash away.

available_choices.description: Let Lady Macbeth return the daggers and blame the sleeping guards.
Carry the daggers yourself and refuse to let her return to the chamber.
Confess your part in Duncan's murder before suspicion can be turned against others.

title: The King Is Dead
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 3 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macduff discovers Duncan's murder. The court searches for an explanation as Malcolm and Donalbain weigh their safety.
opening_narration: A cry tears through the castle. Duncan is found dead, and every face turns toward the nearest explanation.

available_choices.description: Support the accusation against Duncan's guards before questions turn toward you.
Acknowledge that the guards may be innocent and help Malcolm and Donalbain leave safely.

title: A Crown in the Balance
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 4 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Malcolm and Donalbain depart under suspicion and threat. The nobles consider who can hold Scotland together.
opening_narration: The princes leave the court. Their flight is read as guilt by some and prudence by others; the crown waits.

available_choices.description: Accept the crown and promise order, despite the unanswered questions.
Invite Malcolm to return under protection and relinquish your claim.

title: The Uneasy Crown
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 4 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth is crowned, but Banquo's knowledge and the unstable succession trouble his new rule.
opening_narration: The crown settles on my head. Its weight is less than the thought of who may inherit it.

available_choices.description: Keep Banquo close and answer his doubts with candor.
Keep Banquo at a distance and learn what he knows before the feast.

title: The Heirs of Banquo
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 3, Scene 1 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth learns that the Weird Sisters promised a royal future to Banquo's descendants and fears his crown may be temporary.
opening_narration: I have the crown, yet the prophecy gives its long future to Banquo's line. Fear begins to speak as policy.

available_choices.description: Hire assassins to kill Banquo and Fleance before the feast.
Refuse to murder your friend and confront the prophecy openly.

title: The Road to the Feast
location: A wooded road near the palace
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 3, Scene 3 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: The hired men attack Banquo's party. Fleance's fate determines whether Banquo's prophecy remains a living threat.
opening_narration: The hired men wait in the dark. Before the feast, I will know whether fear has bought me peace.

available_choices.description: Banquo is killed, but Fleance escapes into the night.
The attack fails; Banquo escapes with Fleance and may expose the plot.
Banquo is killed and Fleance is captured alive.

title: The King's Feast
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 3, Scene 4 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: At the feast, Macbeth's response depends on whether Banquo survived the attack; the nobles watch the king closely.
opening_narration: The feast begins under candlelight. I search each face for the one answer I cannot command.

available_choices.description: Banquo was killed. A vision of him appears; acknowledge what the court has seen.
Banquo was killed. Conceal your terror and let Lady Macbeth dismiss the disturbance.
Banquo survived. Offer him a public place at court and hear his warning.

title: The Empty Chair
location: The great hall, after the guests withdraw
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 3, Scene 4 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: The ghost has shaken Macbeth's authority. Lady Macbeth attempts to contain the damage while the nobles reconsider their allegiance.
opening_narration: The chair is empty now, but the fear remains visible in every guest who has left.

available_choices.description: Tell Lady Macbeth that guilt and fear have begun to rule you.
Reject Lady Macbeth's counsel and tighten control of the court.

title: A Kingdom of Watchers
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 3, Scene 6 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Nobles notice Macbeth's instability. Banquo's survival or death and the treatment of Macduff shape the opposition.
opening_narration: The lords measure every word. I can answer their fear with listening or make fear the only law.

available_choices.description: Seek the Weird Sisters again, while allowing Macduff to travel to England.
Allow Macduff to travel to England rather than seize him.
Detain Macduff and force his household to answer for his disloyalty.

title: The Cave of Warnings
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 4, Scene 1 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: The Weird Sisters show Macbeth visions and warnings. The words are real, but Macbeth must decide how much certainty they grant.
opening_narration: The air turns cold. The apparitions speak in riddles that promise safety while naming danger.

available_choices.description: Trust the warnings as guarantees and act before Macduff can challenge you.
Treat the visions as riddles, not permission to harm an innocent household.

title: A House Without Its Lord
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 4, Scene 2 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth's order reaches Macduff's home. The household faces danger while Macduff is away or held elsewhere.
opening_narration: The order is in my hand. A family stands between my fear and the justice I claim to defend.

available_choices.description: Carry out the order against Macduff's household.
Withdraw the order and leave Macduff's family unharmed.

title: A Dispatch from England
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 4, Scene 3 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Reports from England describe Malcolm testing Macduff's loyalty. Macbeth must decide whether to answer their growing cooperation with negotiation or force.
opening_narration: A dispatch from England names Malcolm and Macduff together. I have not seen their meeting, but I know what their alliance could mean for Scotland.

available_choices.description: Accept Malcolm and Macduff's terms for cooperation and a just restoration of Scotland.
Reject their terms and prepare to hold power against the resistance.
Keep Macduff detained and reject Malcolm's appeal before it can gather support.
Release the captured Fleance as part of an agreement to relinquish the crown.

title: A Cause in Scotland
location: The English camp and the Scottish border
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 4, Scene 3 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: The resistance gathers support. Whether the Macduff family was harmed and whether the alliance holds shape the cause.
opening_narration: A cause can free Scotland, or replace one fear with another. The soldiers wait for the purpose of their march.

available_choices.description: Join the campaign and gather Scottish nobles behind Malcolm.
Offer Macbeth a negotiated abdication before the army advances.
Refuse compromise and let distrust divide the resistance.

title: The Candle at Night
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 1 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Lady Macbeth walks in her sleep, burdened by the bloodshed. Macbeth must decide whether to hear her or shut her away.
opening_narration: A candle moves through the dark. Lady Macbeth speaks to stains no physician can see, and I cannot meet her eyes.

available_choices.description: Stay with Lady Macbeth and seek help without exposing her to the court.
Keep her apart and prepare for the advancing army alone.

title: The Wood That Moves
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 5 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Malcolm's soldiers advance using branches as camouflage. Macbeth sees Birnam Wood moving and must choose defense or retreat.
opening_narration: The hillside seems to move. The prophecy's safety becomes a question, not a shield.

available_choices.description: Hold the castle and trust the prophecy despite the moving wood.
Withdraw to spare the city and preserve a chance to negotiate.

title: The Last Terms
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 7 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: The siege closes around the castle. Macbeth can surrender, negotiate, or risk one final battle.
opening_narration: The gates shake. I may still choose what Scotland inherits from this night.

available_choices.description: Surrender the crown and ask Malcolm to spare the people of Dunsinane.
Accept a settlement that ends the fighting and restores Scotland's council.
Meet Macduff in combat rather than let another decide your fate.

title: The Last Battle
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 8 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth faces Macduff. The outcome depends on earlier violence, the rebellion, and Macbeth's final decision.
opening_narration: Macduff stands before me. The last prophecy no longer sounds like certainty; it sounds like a choice.

available_choices.description: Fight Macduff to the end, refusing surrender.
Lay down your weapon and let Macduff judge you before Scotland.
Use the confusion to flee while Fleance's surviving line carries the prophecy onward.
Break the rebellion's resolve and keep the crown by force.

title: The King Wakes
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 2 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth refuses regicide. The crown remains with Duncan, but the marriage and the prophecy are changed by the refusal.
opening_narration: Duncan wakes to the alarm. I have chosen conscience, though I do not know what that choice will cost.

title: A Confession Before the Crown
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 2, Scene 3 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth admits his role before the nobles can crown him; the truth costs him power but prevents a false accusation.
opening_narration: I speak before the court can invent another story. My name is ruined, but the lie ends here.

title: The Council Restored
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 9 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth relinquishes sole rule under a negotiated settlement, avoiding a final battle and returning authority to a Scottish council.
opening_narration: The crown leaves my hands by agreement. Scotland must now build a rule no single fear can command.

title: Judgment at Scone
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 9 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth survives and submits to judgment. Malcolm restores the throne while the court weighs mercy against justice.
opening_narration: I live to answer for what I have done. The crown is gone; the reckoning is not.

title: The Crown Broken
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 8 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macduff defeats Macbeth, Malcolm takes the crown, and the surviving nobles face the damage left by tyranny.
opening_narration: The crown falls with me. Scotland will outlive my fear, though it cannot undo the blood already shed.

title: The Crown Passes On
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 8 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth escapes the battle, but Fleance's survival leaves Banquo's prophecy alive and Macbeth without a kingdom.
opening_narration: I leave the crown behind. Somewhere beyond the border, Banquo's line still has a future I could not command.

title: A Crown of Ash
canonical_reference: Macbeth, Act 5, Scene 8 (original game prose; events adapted, not Shakespeare dialogue).
summary: Macbeth retains power after crushing the rebellion, but Scotland is ruled through fear and the royal household is fractured.
opening_narration: I keep the crown, and lose the country that gave it meaning. No prophecy can make this peace.
